Thanks for helping improve this book.

This repository uses [Quarto](https://quarto.org/) to build and maintain the website as a Quarto book.

## Installation of Quarto

Download and install Quarto from <https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/>.

To preview the site locally from R, you can also use the `quarto` R package:

```{r}
#| label: contributing-1
#| eval: false
install.packages("quarto")
```

## Install R dependencies

All R packages used across tutorials are listed in the `DESCRIPTION` file under `Imports`. Please keep dependencies in alphabetical order and keep this file up to date.

To install all dependencies:

```{r}
#| label: contributing-2
#| eval: false
remotes::install_deps()
```

## Project structure

```
EnvironmentalComputing/
├── _quarto.yml         # Book configuration and chapter order
├── index.qmd           # Home page (must stay at root)
├── content/           # All tutorial content, organised by section
│   ├── big-picture/
│   ├── basics/
│   ├── data-literacy/
│   ├── data-visualisation/
│   ├── essential-maths/
│   ├── statistical-methods/
│   ├── dynamic-systems/
│   └── coding-skills/
├── _book/              # Rendered output (do not edit manually)
├── images/             # Shared images used in multiple chapters
└── data/               # Shared datasets used in multiple chapters
```

- `_quarto.yml` controls title, chapter order, and formatting.
- `content/` is where most authoring happens.
- `_book/` is generated output and should not be edited manually.

## Naming and style conventions

Please follow these conventions when creating new files and folders:

- lowercase names
- use `-` hyphens to join words, for example `meta-analysis`
- keep folder names concise (3 words or fewer)
- use common abbreviations where appropriate, for example `glms`

Use the `styler` package to format R code within `.qmd` files:

```{r}
#| label: contributing-3
#| eval: false
styler::style_file("content/coding-skills/functions.qmd")
```

## Anatomy of a page

Each tutorial is a `.qmd` file inside a section folder under `content/`.

At minimum, include a title in the YAML header:

```yaml
---
title: "Title of Your Tutorial"
---
```

Page order is controlled by the `chapters:` list in `_quarto.yml`.

## Images and data: where to store files

Use a section-level structure throughout `content/`.

For each first-level section folder (for example `content/statistical-methods/`, `content/data-visualisation/`, `content/misc/`), keep:

- chapter files (`.qmd`) at the section root
- images in `images/`
- local datasets and other data files in `data/`

### Standard layout

```
content/
  statistical-methods/
    linear-models.qmd
    t-tests.qmd
    images/
      One_sample_t_test_image.png
    data/
      Interaction_plots.csv
```

### Referencing assets in pages

From a chapter in that same section:

- images: `![](images/example.png)`
- data in code: `read.csv("data/example.csv")`

### Shared assets across multiple sections

If a file is genuinely shared across many sections, it can still live in project-level `images/` or `data/`. Keep this as the exception, not the default.

### Practical guidance

- do not keep loose image/data files at the same level as section `.qmd` files
- avoid `../../` path chains where possible
- use stable section-relative paths (`images/...`, `data/...`)

## Working with git

Recommended workflow:

1. Pull remote changes at the start of your work session.
2. Make changes to relevant `.qmd` files and assets.
3. Stage your changes.
4. Commit with an informative message.
5. Push your branch.

If you hit a merge conflict, contact a maintainer for help.

## Creating a new page

1. Decide which section the new page belongs to.
2. Create a new `.qmd` file in the relevant `content/` subfolder.
3. Add a YAML header with at least `title:`.
4. Add the new file path to `chapters:` in `_quarto.yml`.
5. Write your tutorial content.

## Building and previewing

Render the whole book:

```{r}
#| label: contributing-4
#| eval: false
quarto::quarto_render()
```

Preview with live reloading:

```{r}
#| label: contributing-5
#| eval: false
quarto::quarto_preview()
```

Equivalent terminal commands:

```bash
quarto render
quarto preview
```

## Fast reruns with caching

Use a 3-layer caching strategy:

1. document-level freeze in `_quarto.yml`
2. chunk-level caching for expensive code blocks
3. file-based cache for shared derived datasets

### 1) Document-level freeze

At the project level in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

With `freeze: auto`, Quarto skips re-executing pages whose source has not changed.

### 2) Chunk-level cache for expensive code

For slow chunks, turn cache on explicitly:

```{r}
#| label: fit-big-model
#| cache: true
#| dependson: prep-data
#| cache.extra: !expr file.mtime("data/raw/surveys.csv")

model <- my_expensive_fit(df)
```

Use `dependson` when a chunk relies on earlier work, and use `cache.extra` to invalidate cache when source data changes.

### 3) Cache derived data for reuse across chapters

Write expensive preprocessing outputs once, then read them elsewhere:

```{r}
#| label: build-derived
#| cache: true

dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
derived <- heavy_preprocess(raw_df)
readr::write_rds(derived, "data/derived/cleaned-surveys.rds")
```

```{r}
#| label: contributing-8
cleaned <- readr::read_rds("data/derived/cleaned-surveys.rds")
```

### Caching guidelines

- cache only slow chunks, not every chunk
- set seeds for stochastic code so cached outputs are reproducible
- treat `data/raw/` as read-only and write generated files to `data/derived/`
- clear stale cache if outputs become inconsistent

## Internal links and cross-references

To link to another page within the book, use a path from project root:

```markdown
See the [data manipulation](/content/data-literacy/making-analysis-ready-data.qmd) section.
```

For sections, figures, and tables, use Quarto cross-references (`@sec-`, `@fig-`, `@tbl-`).
